`INV-2` (precommit-first / reachability-before-content): the build-root precommit must be published before any pool content GET/HEAD/PUT of the build's content; the full write ordering stages blobs into local temp files, then makes the edge-bearing manifest body durable via `stageManifest`, then lands the owner event via `precommitAdd`, and only then do blob uploads reach the pool. topic: CAS's transient-vs-terminal exception classifier separates a

topic: CAS's single true read-side correctness hole
canonical_claim: CAS's single true read-side correctness hole (labeled X1/R1, "missing read"): a ref-less/cross-node reader resolves ref to manifest to blob-location at plan time, discards the manifest, then performs a deferred, unpinned blob GET later; if the ref is dropped and GC completes condemn to pending to delete before that GET fires, a committed datum becomes unreadable mid-query (`NoSuchKey`). This is bounded to the write/GC plane being otherwise loss-free; the fix direction is an ephemeral reader pin folded into the GC mark/ack-floor union, or bounding query lifetime below the condemn-to-delete latency.

topic: CAS's security perimeter is exactly the
canonical_claim: CAS's security perimeter is exactly the S3 bucket credential: there is no intra-pool authorization, identities are self-asserted and unsigned, and blobs are shared pool-wide by content hash with no namespace in the blob key. Combined with non-cryptographic CityHash128 content-addressing and reads that never re-verify payload-against-key, this enables SEC-1 (High) collision poisoning: because dedup is HEAD-first and blobs are pool-global, an attacker who can craft a `CityHash128` collision can pre-seed a poisoned blob under the victim's future hash so a victim in a different table/tenant later writing the benign content dedups to the poison and reads attacker bytes, with all CRC checks passing (latent in a single-trust-domain pool, real the moment a pool is multi-tenant).

SEC-8: provenance (`server_id`, timestamp, op, `build_id`) and the `CasEvent` sink give a useful audit trail, but everything is self-asserted and forgeable by a pool-write adversary, so it is good for debugging and honest-fault forensics but not an integrity/attribution control against a malicious insider.

topic: SEC-9: blobs are plaintext table bytes
canonical_claim: SEC-9: blobs are plaintext table bytes; confidentiality relies entirely on S3 SSE + bucket policy + TLS, and content-addressing also makes content equality externally observable (same content maps to the same key), which deployments with confidential data across tenants in one pool should assume as an equality-leakage risk.

Canonical catalog-absent objects are inert debris that must never damage data; fsck therefore needs a grammar-discriminated `janitor_pending` class rather than treating all such debris as a hard corruption finding.

On existing non-CAS disks, immediate local-filesystem visibility and object-storage parts represented as independent files generally prevented the weak disk-transaction contract from causing direct data loss, but MergeTree still depended on implementation-specific visibility and early sub-part commits.

CAS's documented deployment rule from the security audit: never share a CAS pool across trust domains until SEC-1 (collision poisoning), SEC-2 (dedup existence oracle), and SEC-3 (no intra-pool authorization) are addressed; the single highest-leverage code fix common to both the Jepsen-style consistency audit and the security audit is a `writer_epoch`-fenced shard CAS precondition, which simultaneously closes SEC-7 (NTP/pause-amplifiable fencing) and the J1/J2/J3 split-brain class.
The B140 dangle fix requires both build-root protection and fail-closed commit; the model found that either mechanism alone is insufficient.

The holey-list sabotage configuration `_sab_holeylist` of `CaRelinkConfirmCore.tla` violated `ConfirmedRelinkNeverDangles` with one incomplete LIST page, proving that relink confirmation is safe only conditional on LIST completeness.

A namespace can leave the old walk silent when `cursor == RefTxnId{}`, `listing.logs` is empty, and `checkpoints.life_epochs` has no entry; the old code skipped `while (expected)` with no anomaly, hold, or warning, while the current `!grounding` arm emits a warning and records `CheckpointUnusable` or a hold.
The TXN-final phase-3 soak completed with `dangling=0`, recovered from five faults and three restarts, reported `ABORTED-retried INSERT=0`, and drained the pool to 256 bytes.
The S38 late-PUT fence test passed 19 of 19 verdicts and the real object store returned HTTP 412 for a straggler's conditional create at a sealed id.
`CaB140DangleMerge` passed its empty-`Trees` configuration `m_empty_trees.cfg` as green.

In the observed list-incompleteness occurrence, ref-log objects `0x1430c`, `0x1430d`, and `0x1430e` were uploaded in strict ID order at 16:47:19.211480, 16:47:19.212340, and 16:47:19.213680 respectively.
The first walk returned ref-log object `0x1430e` after its upload, but did not return the two earlier objects `0x1430c` and `0x1430d` even though they had been durable for 1.3–2.2 ms at that point.
A measurement of 65,263 ref-log uploads found zero out-of-order uploads after partitioning by writer epoch.
For the observed disagreement, `ch2` deleted zero ref objects over all time, `ch1` deleted zero ref objects during 16:47:00–16:48:00, and `ch2` deleted zero ref objects during that interval.
Relaxing the condemned-token gate for non-pending entries was rejected because `SabotageAdoptRetiredToken` demonstrates that binding a listed token is unsafe.
Accepting a condemned token without resurrecting it is unsound because exact-token GC deletion can graduate and delete that incarnation, leaving the committed manifest dangling.

Skipping the occupancy `HEAD` on a dedup-cache hit is unsafe: the cached matching blob may have had zero in-degree and been fully deleted since caching, and after the proposed §5 change an absent `.meta` object would look like Clean, so only `HEAD` or a body GET can distinguish absence from a live blob.
A fallback is acceptable only when uncertainty concerns the mechanism; uncertainty about the source must abort and retry rather than silently taking another route to the same peer.
CAS code uses `LOGICAL_ERROR` only for genuine programming invariants and uses `CORRUPTED_DATA`, `NETWORK_ERROR`, or `ABORTED` for the corresponding existing CAS error classes.

The primary soak correctness oracle is all-replica agreement on `count() + sum(sipHash64(*))`, with an absolute Python-side prediction for deterministic `INSERT ... SELECT ... FROM numbers(N)` workloads.

The core invariants (INV-NO-LOSS, INV-NO-DANGLE, INV-NO-RETURN, INV-JOURNAL-COVERAGE, MonotoneGC) are model-checked by CaIncarnationCore.tla; mount-safety invariants (WriterEpochMonotoneUnique, SupersededWriterMakesNoMutation) are model-checked by a focused Phase-0 TLA+ model; INV-NO-DANGLING and INV-NO-ORPHAN-EDGE under D1 are model-checked by CaGcShardIncarnationCore.tla (724,944 states, GREEN as of 2026-07-01).

Backend conformance table: AWS S3 (versioning off) uses ETag, fully conforming, validated live 2026-07-03, probe-gated at startup (DeleteObject If-Match GA'd Sep 2025). RustFS 1.0.0-beta.8 uses ETag, empirically verified 2026-06-11, leading open-source CI candidate, with known issue rustfs#3231 (overwrite-leak of objects above the store's inline threshold, e.g. 128 KiB, in unversioned buckets) that can produce metacache LIST storms and false 404s on HEAD -- the only source of GC fold clamps observed to date. Azure Blob uses ETag (write-sensitive), supported and probe-gated, with versioning/soft-delete required off. GCS uses generation, binding specified but implementation deferred, fail-closed until probed. MinIO OSS (archived 2026-02) has If-Match on DELETE silently ignored (confirmed 2026-06-11) -- fail-closed. Ceph RGW has no conditional delete documented -- fail-closed.

The archaeology report names concrete evidence-based test-coverage gaps (vol. 06 §5): the `SingleWriterSlot` background renew loop has zero direct test references (`MountLeaseKeeper` is exercised only via synchronous `renewOnce`, so the async renewal thread and its error-latch split-brain-safety path rest on review plus soak) — flagged High because the P3.1 S13 fence-of-blocked-lease wedge lived exactly in this machinery; `CasGcScheduler` thread pacing/heartbeat cadence is unit-untestable without sleeps and was verified by review only (the P3-B1 wedge was exactly here); async-insert retry row-loss (B139) is parked behind the soak default `async_insert=0` with no gtest; and several `IMetadataStorage` overrides (`createMetadataFile`, `truncateFile`, `chmod`, `setLastModified`, `setReadOnly`, `createDirectory*`) are never driven by any test, though mostly deliberate no-ops.
The reader implementation requires a TLA+ invariant that every object in a live reader pin's `replay(S, tail <= L)` closure is neither condemned nor pruned.

The owner-tombstone change requires tests proving that decommission leaves a present owner object with `retired_at_ms` set, that a competing `putOverwrite` makes the tail abort closed, and that a tombstoned same-UUID owner is rejected by `claimOwnerOrThrow` with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
A detector should flag a namespace whose current catalog life contributes no checkpoint or listed objects while a non-current life of the same name has listed objects.

The TXN-ONE-PIPELINE design's plan-time audits require a fault-injection regression verifying that process termination after a successful `Keeper` publication but before disk `commit` enters the existing missing-part fetch/lost-part path, and explicitly forbid introducing CA-specific recovery for this window.
